clue.text: Garment for drunks?

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting legwear item, a pair of hose worn from waist to toe
people who are tight, an old word for tipsy, turned whimsically into a plural noun

explanation.surface: A question about what clothing suits heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' for drunk is an adjective; the question mark admits that making it a plural noun for drunken people is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery covering the legs and lower body is an everyday piece of clothing.

clue.text: Leaderless council crushed by aunt to the Spanish queen in the 25

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed inside it, so the council goes within the aunt

parts.note: tia is the Spanish word for aunt

indicators.note: losing its leader means the council word drops its first letter

parts.note: the Witan was the assembly of advisers to Anglo-Saxon kings

explanation.surface: A headless committee squashed by a relative on the way to a Spanish monarch in some scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' leaves ITAN, which 'crushed by' puts inside the aunt. 25 is DREAM, so the queen is the fairy queen of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the fairy queen, wife of the fairy king, in Shakespeare's comedy of the enchanted wood.

clue.text: Part of Soviet penal system, partly red and silver

indicators.note: only part of the heraldic colour word is used, its last two letters being dropped

parts.note: gules is the heraldic term for red
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

explanation.surface: A labour camp is described as being part red and part silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' trims GULES to GUL; ES goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was known by this acronym, and each camp was one part of it.

clue.text: Pitched battle over container holding record

indicators.note: the rearranged battle letters lie over and around the container, enclosing it
pitched suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: an urn is a vessel or container

explanation.surface: A fight is staged above a vessel that keeps a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitched' makes TTABLE, and 'over' wraps it round the container after the first T. 'Pitched battle' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'Pitched' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone's rotating platter is the thing on which a vinyl disc sits as it plays.

clue.text: Conservative setter's in business arrangement of 10

indicators.note: the Conservative and the setter's words go inside the business arrangement

parts.note: a deal is a business agreement
the setter is, from the setter's own view, I'M

explanation.surface: A Tory compiler is involved in a commercial deal about the number ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves in the third person, so 'setter's' is 'setter is' and gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal system is based on ten, so the adjective means relating to tens.

clue.text: Far-reaching reductions in army base

definitions.meaning: severe, extensive cuts in spending
A British Army barracks in Surrey

explanation.surface: Severe spending cuts hit a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: Deepcut Barracks in Surrey was a Royal Logistic Corps training base, in the news over deaths of recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe slashing of budgets is described as a profound cutback; Deepcut is also a named British barracks.

clue.text: Immobilisation of one that won't talk quietly

parts.note: someone who clams up is a clam, a person who keeps quiet
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Restraining a silent prisoner, done softly.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheel clamp is the device British traffic wardens fit to immobilise illegally parked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a device that holds something fast, preventing it from moving.

clue.text: 24/6's 25 time

definitions.meaning: the 24th of June's Dream, i.e. the title of Shakespeare's play, of which this phrase is the first part
a period of the year, the shortest dark hours around the solstice

explanation.walkthrough: 24/6 is the date 24 June, Midsummer Day, and 25 is DREAM, so 24/6's 25 is the play title.
explanation.definitionFit: The short darkness of the summer solstice is a well-known moment in the calendar, and the first words of a Shakespeare title.

clue.text: See 21
Honour small boy king in the 25

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Ron is a short form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A youngster is decorated and crowned in some scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is DREAM: the king is the fairy king in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: He rules the fairies in Shakespeare's woodland comedy, married to their queen.

clue.text: Good enough to supply beer to all

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Being decent enough to provide drinks for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the verb; read as 'in a supple manner' it bends BEER TO ALL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable or passable is acceptable without being excellent.

clue.text: A rebellion occurs before time to check

parts.note: UDI, the Unilateral Declaration of Independence by Rhodesia in 1965, was a rebellion against Britain

explanation.surface: An uprising takes place before it is time to inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: An official examination of accounts is an inspection of them.

clue.text: See 6
Get back ecstasy, keeping notes

indicators.note: one word keeps the other inside it, so the notes are held within the ecstasy

parts.note: rapture is intense joy, ecstasy
E and C are musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone tries to regain bliss while holding on to their notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' looks like the drug, which crosswords often make E; here it is the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain is to take possession again of something lost.

clue.text: Fictitious prison where king has a veto on extremes

indicators.note: in an across clue, placing one piece on another puts it after, so the king, a and veto come after the extremes

parts.note: A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
a ban is a prohibition, a veto

explanation.surface: A jail where the monarch can forbid things at the limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison is the wizard jail in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the wizards' jail guarded by dementors in J K Rowling's novels, an invented place.

clue.text: Pub removed by Cromwell?

definitions.meaning: a common British pub name
Cromwell's regime had the head of King Charles I cut off

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tavern was closed by the Lord Protector.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I was beheaded in 1649 under Cromwell; the King's Head is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Many British inns bear this name on their sign, and a monarch's head was literally removed under Cromwell.

clue.text: Bits of thread on guitar?

definitions.meaning: loose fringe ends of yarn left on a loom
strums idly on strings

explanation.surface: Some scraps of yarn are found on a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Weavers call the unwoven ends of warp yarn by this name; as a verb it also means strumming idly.

clue.text: Fool in cry of 14 whose 19 across helped forward 21 7's 25

indicators.note: the fool goes inside the cry

parts.note: a roar is a loud cry
a sap is a fool, a dupe
14 down is the pub clue, whose first word is the monarch's possessive, shortened as K (king) plus the 'S

explanation.surface: A fool shouting in a pub honours the woman whose bus journey advanced a famous civil-rights vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is BUS TRIP and 21 7 is the civil rights leader, so the definition is the woman whose bus protest advanced his vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Her 1955 refusal to give up a bus seat in Montgomery sparked the boycott that advanced the civil-rights leader's vision.

clue.text: French city makes blood boil

definitions.meaning: a city in the Loire valley in western France
infuriates

explanation.surface: A town in France is infuriating.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire city shares its spelling with the verb meaning enrages.

clue.text: Person in charge is the one with the rope

definitions.meaning: a captain or leader
someone using a skipping rope

explanation.surface: The boss is the one holding the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's captain or team leader is in charge; and someone jumping a rope is also so called.

clue.text: Epitaph on bankrupt that had outing on public transport

indicators.note: the epitaph goes on the bankrupt, placed after it as an inscription follows a name

parts.note: bust means broke, bankrupt
RIP, rest in peace, is a common gravestone epitaph

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription for a ruined man who had been on an excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that had' joins the wordplay to the definition; the surface is a gravestone joke about a ruined traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion by coach or omnibus is a journey on public transport.

clue.text: Bed that had a 25

definitions.meaning: the floor of a river or sea
Nick the weaver in Shakespeare's play, who wakes saying he has had a most rare vision

explanation.walkthrough: 25 is DREAM: Nick Bottom the weaver speaks of his dream in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverbed is the lowest part, the foot, of the water; Shakespeare's weaver bears the same name.

clue.text: NCO half back that is a star

indicators.note: back reads the shortened word in reverse order
only half of the rank word is kept, its last four letters going

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: A sergeant-type figure who is half-back is a sporting star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts CORPORAL to CORP and 'back' turns it into PROC. 'half back' looks like a sports position.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the brightest star in Canis Minor, the Little Dog.

clue.text: King with a 25 suffers terminal hurt

indicators.note: the words suffer damage, so their letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch with a vision suffers a fatal wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is DREAM: the King with a dream is the US civil rights leader of the 'I have a dream' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The civil rights leader surnamed King famously declared 'I have a dream' in 1963.

clue.text: Beckett's revising suits Bard

indicators.note: revising the words reworks their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Samuel Beckett is rewriting work that suits Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beckett's' is read as 'Beckett is': the playwright of Waiting for Godot belongs to the Theatre of the Absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett was a leading writer of the Theatre of the Absurd, so he is classed as one of its practitioners.

clue.text: Being quiet during dance will be off-putting

indicators.note: the quiet sign comes during the dance, inside it

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Keeping silent in the middle of a dance will put people off.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive away or disgust, to be unappealing.

clue.text: Boy from Madrid stopped rot

indicators.note: the boy's name comes from within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A Spanish lad halted decay.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits in 'stopPED ROt'; 'Madrid' signals a Spanish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedro is a common Spanish boy's name, the equivalent of Peter.

clue.text: Something very pleasant caused endless trauma to 21 7

definitions.meaning: a delight, a lovely thing
trauma without its last letter is Traum, German for the night vision, which is what the German reformer would call it

explanation.walkthrough: 21 7 is Martin Luther, the German reformer: to him TRAUM(a) is German for this.
explanation.definitionFit: A delightful thing is called a perfect vision of delight; Traum is the German word for it.

clue.text: Belgian port deprived of article by pipsqueak

indicators.note: the port loses the article from its letters

parts.note: Antwerp is a major port in Belgium
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A small, insignificant person has robbed a Belgian harbour of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a silly, insignificant person.

clue.text: Decorum connected with ownership?

definitions.meaning: correct behaviour, seemliness
read as the state of being a proprietor, an owner

explanation.surface: Good manners linked to owning things.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly behaviour is decorum; the word also once meant property and ownership.

clue.text: Lumpy with nearly all round effect

indicators.note: read as a verb, to effect is to bring about, so the letters are worked into a new form
nearly all of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Bumpy, with an almost total rounding effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' leaves AL, and 'effect', read as a verb meaning bring about, reworks AL with the round letters; the surface reading of effect as a noun misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in small knobs or swellings is lumpy.

clue.text: Danish invaders decapitate people of letters

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, the first letter

parts.note: postmen are people who deliver letters

explanation.surface: Viking raiders behead literary figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people of letters' looks like writers; it means mail carriers. The Ostmen were Norse settlers in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostmen, east men, was the name for Scandinavian settlers and raiders in medieval Ireland.
